title: Six Stars, 13 Years: Jordan, Brady & Mantle Card Price Growth
summary: How much have iconic cards grown since 2013? We track 13-year price changes for Michael Jordan, Tom Brady, Charizard, Mickey Mantle, and LeBron James.
body_markdown:
The last installment of arguably the most popular video game of all time came out on September 17th, 2013. Three days later, it passed $1 billion in sales. Now, after 13 years, the game’s next installment is finally here.


A lot has changed over the past decade-plus, and in a space that moves as quickly as cards, today’s market looks a whole lot different than it did 13 years ago. While superstars like[Tom Brady](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Tom%20Brady&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) have since retired, market movers like the former New England and Tampa Bay quarterback, along with icons like[Michael Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Wayne Gretzky](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Wayne%20Gretzky&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Mickey Mantle](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Mickey%20Mantle&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , and[LeBron James](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=LeBron%20James&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) —and pocket monsters like[Charizard](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Charizard&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) —continue to dictate the price of cards across categories.


To chart out just how big of a change The Hobby has seen over that time, we identified six legendary cards that typically set the benchmark for their sport or game and compared their prices in 2013 to their value today.

Whether you’re busy driving around the streets of Vice City, flying throughout Leonida, or chasing bounties in[Courtyard’s Most Wanted event](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/blog-courtyard-most-wanted?) , things look a bit different these days. Time to steal a car, tune into your favorite radio station, and get ready for a blast from the past.


## **The Benchmark Cards: 2013 vs. 2026**


### **1952 Topps #311**[Mickey Mantle](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Mickey%20Mantle&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **(PSA 8)**


Mantle’s first Topps card is the standard for postwar[baseball cards](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=baseball) . Back in May 2013, one of just two PSA 8.5 copies[sold for $272,550](https://collectrea.com/archives/2013/Spring/3/1952-topps-311-mickey-mantle-psa-nm-mt-85) at Robert Edwards Auctions. A year later, a PSA 8[sold for $179,250](https://collectrea.com/archives/2014/Fall/526/1952-topps-311-mickey-mantle-gai-nm-mt-8) .


In June 2026, a PSA 8[sold for $1.83 million](https://www.si.com/collectibles/mantle-mania-record-prices-mickey-mantle-cards-and-magazine) at Goldin, followed by another—[that carried a silver Mike Baker Authenticated sticker](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/mickey-mantle-card-sets-record-222414462.html) —at $3.721 million via Heritage Auctions in August. The collectors that bought 13 years ago must be smiling ear to ear.


### **1979 O-Pee-Chee #18**[Wayne Gretzky](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Wayne%20Gretzky&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **(PSA 9)**


The Gretzky O-Pee-Chee is[hockey](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=hockey) ’s benchmark rookie card. Back in the early 2010s, PSA 9s[averaged around $5,000](https://www.sportscollectorsdaily.com/lone-psa-10-o-pee-chee-gretzky-rookie-card-set-auction/) . A PSA 9 of the same card[sold for $136,640](https://www.psacard.com/spec/psa/321695?g=9) at Goldin in June 2026, a roughly 27x increase.


Only two PSA 10 copies exist. One[sold for $1.29 million](https://sportscollectorsdigest.com/news/wayne-gretzky-rookie-card-record-sale-heritage-auctions) at Heritage Auctions in December 2020, the first hockey card to pass $1 million, and a PSA 10 later[sold for a whopping $3.75 million](https://sportscollectorsdigest.com/news/wayne-gretzky-rookie-card-record-sale-heritage-auctions) in May 2021.


### **1986 Fleer #57**[Michael Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **(PSA 10)**


Jordan first took the floor for the Chicago Bulls in 1984, yet his 1986 Fleer card is widely considered his true rookie given the limited availability of the ‘84 print, which was only available in team bags and limited sets.


Both are worth a pretty penny, but a PSA 10 of the ‘86 card[sold for $10,463 in 2013](https://www.psacard.com/Lists/top-15-modern-card-prices) , and 13 years later, a PSA 10 of the same card[sold for $414,800](https://www.cardladder.com/ladder/card/1986-fleer-michael-jordan-base-57-psa-10) —a nearly 40x increase. However, that price pales in comparison to the[$2.7 million](https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46673686/michael-jordan-card-sets-aftermarket-record-27m-sale) a PSA 9 of the ‘86 #57 sold for in 2025, with the additional cost stemming from the card’s PSA 10 auto.


### **1999 Pokémon Base Set 1st Edition Holo**[Charizard](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Charizard&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **#4 (PSA 10)**


Charizard is the only non-athlete on this list (depending on who you ask), so he’s getting a different treatment. Back in 2017, the fifth installment of the video game franchise overhauled its online mode with new content. That same year a PSA 10 Charizard[sold for $20,100](https://www.psacard.com/spec/psa/544028) . In October 2026, a PSA 10 of the same card[closed for $1.38 million](https://polkastarter.com/blog/first-edition-charizard-psa-10-1380000-fanatics) .


### **2003 Topps Chrome #111**[LeBron James](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=LeBron%20James&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **(PSA 10)**


Meanwhile, LeBron is the only athlete on the list that has yet to retire, as he continues his quest for another ring with the Philadelphia 76ers. Back in September 2017, the year of the famous multiplayer update—and a year after winning a third ring—a 2003 Topps Chrome #111 LeBron James PSA 10 could be had for just[$770](https://www.psacard.com/spec/psa/363521?g=10) . In November 2026, a PSA 10 of the same card[sold for $12,500](https://www.psacard.com/spec/psa/363521?g=10) . It’s The King’s 24th season in[the NBA](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=basketball) , and he’s still among[the most-searched basketball players on Courtyard](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/most-popular-nba-cards-and-courtyard-marketplace-data) .


### **2000 Playoff Contenders #144**[Tom Brady](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Tom%20Brady&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **Rookie Ticket Autograph (PSA 10)**


Brady is the only other athlete that was still playing when the latest edition of the video game franchise was released. The then-Patriots QB’s rookie autograph is the football card all others are valued against, and back in 2017, the year of his famous 28-3 Super Bowl victory, a PSA 10[sold for $85,000](https://www.psacard.com/spec/psa/294008?g=10) . In June 2025, the same card at the same grade[sold for $208,483](https://www.psacard.com/spec/psa/294008?g=10) , about 2.5x the price, while a numbered Championship Ticket version[sold in a PSA 8 for $854,000](https://www.si.com/collectibles/a-historic-f1-sale-leads-top-5-sports-card-sales-of-week) in October 2026. Only 13 PSA 10s of Brady’s 2000 Playoff Contenders Rookie Ticket Autograph exist, making sales rare, but a PSA 9 sold in September 2026 for[$150,000](https://www.psacard.com/spec/psa/294008?g=9) .


## **What 13 Years of Trading Card Growth Tells Us**


Each and every one of the six famed cards is worth far more than it was when the fifth edition of the landmark video game debuted…and not by a small margin, either. Gains range from roughly 2.5x for the[Brady](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Tom%20Brady&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , to roughly 69x for the[Charizard](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Charizard&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) .


However, not all of these card markets are at their peak, with Jordan’s market currently below 2021’s record-setting year. Some of this can be explained via the pop counts of the cards; there are just two PSA 10s of[Gretzky’s](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Wayne%20Gretzky&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) most famous rookie card compared to nearly 2,500 of LeBron’s.


As time goes on, which direction do you think the market for each of these cards/players will trend?


## **Chase Your Next Grail on Courtyard**


What will likely go down as the biggest video game release of all time is underway, a launch 13 years in the making.


Whether you’re[collecting the game’s in-game trading cards](https://www.nss-sports.com/en/news/47745/gta-6-sports-trading-cards) , chasing bounties in[Courtyard’s Most Wanted event](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=limited_drop) , or eyeing an IRL[Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Brady](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Tom%20Brady&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , or[Gretzky](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Wayne%20Gretzky&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) of your own, Courtyard’s got ways to chase all six of these icons, from the 1951 Bowman #253 Mickey Mantle (SGC 4 VG-EX) found in the[Baseball Legend Pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/baseball-legend-pack) , to the 2000 Upper Deck Gold Reserve #215 Tom Brady (BGS 9 MINT) in the[Football Ultra Pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/football-ultra-pack) , and many more. For those that want to lock in on a specific target,[Courtyard's marketplace](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) has plenty of cards to chase, too—including[a 1985 Star Last 11 ROY's #1 Michael Jordan (BGS 8.5 NM-MT+)](https://courtyard.io/asset/f93f87903cd5f492a11229d8fe81d4eaf753fcc5416b8c3543530dbd36a5136b) that's just waiting for someone to make an offer.


Time to accept the mission, rack up some stars, and get collecting!
